raw_response:
**My reasoning:**

I've worked this land for 40 years. I know what works here in Quzhou. The wheat-maize rotation is the backbone — reliable buyers, stable prices, and I can manage it mostly myself. Cotton is getting harder. My son works in the city now, so at harvest time I'm short on hands, and picking cotton at my age is brutal. I'm keeping cotton but cutting it down to 3 mu — just enough to make it worthwhile without breaking my back.

For wheat and maize I'll use improved and hybrid seeds like I have for the past 15 years. The yield difference is real. I'm not going back to traditional varieties.

Fertilizer — I've learned to put down a solid base application and then top-dress. I don't chase the maximum recommendation. I've seen neighbors burn crops and waste money. My rates are what I've settled on after decades. For cotton I go heavier on potassium — it matters for boll set.

Water is my biggest worry. The well is working but groundwater here has been dropping my whole life. I irrigate at critical stages only — I don't flood unless the crop needs it.

Tillage: I rotary till before wheat, skip deep tillage on maize because the wheat stubble stays and the soil is fine. For cotton I'll plough — I need a clean seedbed.

Pesticides: cotton gets more sprays because of bollworm and aphids. Wheat and maize I keep it lean unless I see a real problem.
